newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close up on stronger beef ideas.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close up on stronger beef ideas.

text.p: Expectations of increased beef demand, partly from the Taiwan pork export ban, kept CME live cattle futures mostly strong at the close, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.450 to 0.025 cent per lb higher with April up 0.075 at 68.175 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.300 higher to 0.050 lower with May up 0.025 at 69.100 cents.

Although recent weak beef prices have curbed packer demand for cattle, expectations are for both domestic and export demand for beef to strengthen. Domestic demand for beef was seen increasing after Easter and export demand could rise if beef replaces Taiwan pork on Pacific Rim consumers' tables.

Demand for U.S. beef may rise to replace some of the pork that will be unavailable due to the pork export ban in Taiwan. Beef supplies are seen plentiful through the summer, based on the last Cattle-on-Feed report, and this will make beef competative if pork prices rise further, they said.

But packer demand for fed cattle was uncertain over the next couple of weeks which added to rolling of longs and kept a lid on April. Traders were beginning to talk about packers growing short of cattle for near-term operations but they noted previously-contracted supplies for April delivery will be available next week.
Refco and LFG sold April late and RBH was a notable buyer of June. Prudential Securities spread long June/short April late. E.D.& F. Man spread the opposite early, sources said.
In live cattle options, RBH bought June 64 calls and Iowa Grain bought April 69 calls. Commission houses did the 68/67 April put spread, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle showed spillover support from stronger deferred live cattle but traded uneven as corn futures also traded mostly higher, traders said.
"The market was caught between a friendly live cattle market and higher corn futures," said Julia Bussie of AG Edwards.
Recent strength in cash feeders and a higher index lent support while spreading of short feeders against long live cattle futures also limited the gain, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index rose $0.03 to $69.35 per cwt.

LFG sold May early before spreading of long May/short September by Stone Traders. Cargill Investor Services notably spread long October live cattle/short April feeders, long February live cattle/short October feeders and long March feeders/short June live cattle, pit sources said.
